messages:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: p99 tail latency breach on streaming-api in eu-west-2 (detected 03:21 UTC) - SLO p99=200ms, current ~1.2s. Triggered alert group 'streaming.tail.latency'.

oncall-jen: saw the page, I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking recent deploys.

matt (sre): I already started a `tcpdump` on the edge proxies. initial observation: a lot of retransmits on connections to NAT gateways in az-b and az-c.

alex (infra): confirming increased SYN+RST counts on the nat instances. checking SNAT ephemeral port exhaustion metrics now.

jon-deploy (deploy-bot): deploy 2026.03.15-1242 rolled to eu-west-2 (streaming-proxy v3.14). No immediate rollback.

jen: can we rule out an app-level regression? tanya, any schema/codec changes to streaming framing?

 tanya (eng-runtime): no framing changes in this deploy. heatmap of request sizes looks similar. suspect network-level.

matt (sre): timeline: p50/p95 were stable, p99 spiked ~03:19 UTC and incidents started at 03:21. Streaming stalls correlate with TLS handshake retries for ~5-10% of connections.

alex (infra): DNS query latency to our resolver also spiked at same time for eu-west-2: 50ms -> 800ms for names that are NAT targets. attaching snippet from graphs:
```
zone: eu-west-2 | dns_query_latency_95: 48ms -> 810ms
nat_ephemeral_util: 62% -> 98%
syn_retransmit_rate: 0.2% -> 4.8%
```

matt (sre): logs show a rash of `ECONNRESET` and `handshake timeout` on streaming-proxy. Stack traces point to TLS handshake stalls.

jen: customer impact? csm-ryan pls summarize immediate customer reports.

csm-ryan: three customers on dedicated capacity reported increased stalls and aborted streams. One support ticket from a high-traffic customer showing repeated reconnects. No full outage, but degraded UX.

jen: ok, mitigation path options: 1) failover traffic to eu-west-1 for affected routes, 2) add more NAT instances / rotate ports, 3) throttle large concurrent handshakes at proxy to reduce tail. preferences?

alex (infra): we can spin up two additional NAT instances in az-b in ~6-8 min (auto-scaling hit limit). That will buy us breathing room for ephemeral ports. I'll start that now.

matt (sre): while that's in progress, do we want to toggle handshake timeout lower on the streaming-proxy to fail faster and avoid long stalls? risk: more transient disconnects for slow connections.

 tanya (eng-runtime): we have a config flag `tls_handshake_max_ms` on the proxy that can be lowered from 10s -> 3s via config rollout. rolling that to 10% first. I'll enqueue a canary.

jen: do it. set the rollout target to non-customer-facing nodes? canary on internal only.

 tanya (eng-runtime): doing canary: `curl -XPOST https://console/api/rollouts -d '{"service":"streaming-proxy","config":{"tls_handshake_max_ms":3000},"target":"canary-internal"}'`

deploy-bot: rollout started for streaming-proxy config -> canary-internal (id: r-20260315-01).

matt (sre): started `tcpdump` and `ss -s` on proxies. seeing many CLOSE_WAIT and retransmit spikes inbound to nat. packets show reordering and TCP dup ACKs.

alex (infra): NAT instances are now at 99% ephemeral ports exhausted for some backends. spinning up new NATs and enabling port range expansion in the firewall/NAT rules. Command: `terraform apply -target=module.nat.eu-west-2.extra_instances` (I'm on it).

jen: great. also please add temporary routing rule to prefer intra-az routes when possible to avoid cross-zone hairpinning. alex, can you push a route policy?

alex (infra): yes, pushing policy `prefer_local_az=true` to k8s netpolicy-controller for streaming subnets. will take ~2min to propagate.

matt (sre): early telemetry after canary: p99 dropping from 1.2s -> 420ms on canary nodes. connection failure rate slightly up but handshake latencies improved.

csm-ryan: letting customers know we're mitigating. sending templated note: "We are investigating increased streaming latency in eu-west-2, mitigation in progress. Expect intermittent reconnects."

jen: note customer comms in thread. also create a post-incident action: why did ephemeral port consumption spike? are we leaking sockets or a downstream DDoS?

 tanya (eng-runtime): rolling config to 50% while infra finishes NAT capacity ramp. will monitor error budget.

alex (infra): extra NATs live. ephemeral exhaustion dropped to 45% within 120s. DNS latency normalized.

matt (sre): p99 now ~260ms cluster-wide, streaming stalls decreased by ~85%. marking customer-impact as "degraded" -> moving to "mitigated".

jen: handing off to post-mortem/restore rotation. oncall-jen -> handoff to matt for follow-ups. matt, can you own postmortem and action items?

matt (sre): taking handoff. immediate action items: 1) audit NAT port usage patterns, 2) add runbook step to pre-scale nat pools during high-handshake windows, 3) add alert for ephemeral port exhaustion >80%, 4) investigate whether streaming clients retried too aggressively.

jen: thank you. final status update to #incidents: mitigation succeeded, partial customer impact, root cause suspected: sudden spike in concurrent TLS handshakes + insufficient NAT ephemeral capacity -> packet loss/retransmits -> p99 tail spike. follow-ups assigned.

sre-bot: Incident `INC-20260315-2174500000` status -> mitigated at 03:38 UTC.

matt (sre): I'll schedule a 30min follow-up postmortem at 09:00 UTC and invite infra, runtime, and csm.

csm-ryan: I'll push a customer update after postmortem outcomes.

jen: great work team. closing the active paging loop. :thumbsup:
